Property.Name: AttachAsROR
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates if the Document to be attached will be set as ROR

Property.Name: AttachedDocument
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the newly created or resolved document attached, used for history summary / it is also used to retrieve selctin values for document in the web form, for when the user assigns an existing document

Property.Name: AttachedFileExtension
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Attached File Extension reference, used to store it to History

Property.Name: AttachedFileName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the File attached to the NDO, RDO or Container, used for History

Property.Name: AttachmentType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration used to indicate what type of document attachment will be perfomed: 1 - Attach a new document that will not be reused (no Revision needed) 2 - Attach a new document that will be reused (Revision must be provided) 3 - Attach an existing document

Property.Name: CalledExternally
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value indicates if the Txn has been called from an external form in the Web, meaning that the ObjectType (not provided) will be resolved based on the Object Instance

Property.Name: ContainerInstance
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object used to get the information and ID of the selected Container instance and save it to history

Property.Name: DocTransactionDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Attach Document Transaction date, used to save in history, be able to order transactions and help in reporting

Property.Name: DocumentDescription
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field allows the user to enter more information about the document

Property.Name: DocumentName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the Document being Attached. This field is Visible when the user chooses Attach a new document that will not be reused or Attach a new document that will be reused.

Property.Name: DocumentProxy
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used to validate the resolved object, this is used by Attach Document for validation purposes

Property.Name: DocumentRevision
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Document Revision being Attached. This field is only visible when user chooses Attach a new document that will be reused.

Property.Name: FilePath
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: External identifier for a document (Path and file name, URL, etc.) Path for the document being uploaded. This field is visible when user chooses Attach a new document that will not be reused or Attach a new document that will be reused.

Property.Name: Identifier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: External identifier for the document (Path and file name, URL, etc.)

Property.Name: InstanceIsROR
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field indictaes if the Revisioned Instance to wich the document is attached to is ROR

Property.Name: InstanceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The instance name of the object that the document is being attached to

Property.Name: InstanceRevision
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The revision of the revisioned object that the document is being attached to

Property.Name: isAttachedImage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Image being attached

Property.Name: IsContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used to determine if the object to attach the document to is a Container, this is used in the Web Page

Property.Name: IsDefect
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates if the Object Type to which a document is being attached is a Defect.

Property.Name: IsDetached
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used to map the Is Detached field to History, by default always false

Property.Name: isIsImage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating the doc being attached is an Image

Property.Name: IsNDO
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used to determine if the object to attach the document to is an NDO, this is used in the Web Page

Property.Name: IsRDO
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used to determine if the object to attach the document to is an RDO, this is used in the Web Page

Property.Name: ObjectInstance
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object used to get the information and ID of the selected Container, NDO or RDO instance and save it to history

Property.Name: ObjectType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration used to identify what type of object a document is being attached to

Property.Name: ObjectTypeId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The CDO type Id for the object. List of all NDO, RDO, and Container objects.

Property.Name: ObjectTypeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the Object Type Name, needed to resolve the value when no access is available to the Object Type's Id

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: ServiceTypeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the Service Type Name that is sent by the page calling the txn from an external form, it is only used when CalledExternally = true

Property.Name: UseROR
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates if the Document attached will be using the Revision of Record

NavigationProperty.Name: DocumentMaint
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Service used to create the Documents to be attached

NavigationProperty.Name: isImageMaint
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Maint service to use when creating an "image" document

NavigationProperty.Name: NamedDataObjectMaint
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Object used to resolve the Object type for an NDO when the txn is called externally

NavigationProperty.Name: RevisionedObjectMaint
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Object used to resolve the Object type for an RDO when the txn is called externally

Property.Name: NewInspectionLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each instance of this object maintains a set of quantity ranges and their associated Lot Size Code to be assigned to a Sample Plan.

Property.Name: NewSampleRateCounterValue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the value that the current Sample Rate is changed to when the transaction is submitted. This field is limited to numeric values.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ResetInspectionLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This Boolean field allows the user to reset the current inspection level of the selected Sampling Current Status record back to the value defined in the Sample Plan modeling object.

Property.Name: SamplingCurrentStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to track the current status of a products sampling plan

Property.Name: ServiceDetails
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Service Details is a holding object for processing.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Document Entry is used to include a Document in a Document and provide a description for it within the Document Set. If there is more than one Document within a Document Set when a request is made to display a Document Set, the list of Document Entries is used to build a selection list. (Note that a one-to-one relationship between a Document Set and a Document is likely the common scenario).

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Selected Resource for the MfgOperation

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: WorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The set of documents associated to a specified MfgOrder, Product, Spec

NavigationProperty.Name: isOrderChangeComments
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Change comment on a Preactor scheduled order

NavigationProperty.Name: MfgOperationHistory
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: History Summary for MfgOperation service to hold comments per MfgOrder, Resource and WorlflowStep

NavigationProperty.Name: MfgOrderList
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: List of Mfg Orders that can be performed on a specified Resource.

Property.Name: isContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of Container stored in the inventory location.

Property.Name: isContainerInLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Will be true if Container is already in an Inventory Location or Material Queue

Property.Name: isContainerLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.

Property.Name: isDefaultInventoryLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Default Inventory Location from Factory.

Property.Name: isExpirationDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expiration Date

Property.Name: isIgnoreErrorsNoExecute
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Specifies that no error should be thrown, but the transaction will not execute. This is used by the ContainerTxn to allow Movement to occur but not put the Container in an Inventory Location - since it is already in one, or in a Material Queue

Property.Name: isInventoryLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Inventory location the materials are being stored, removed, or updated in.

Property.Name: isLot

Property.Name: isLotExist
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean to check is lot exist in inventory location

Property.Name: isName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Container or Lot name of the material located in the inventory location.

Property.Name: isProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Product stored in the inventory location.

Property.Name: isQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Quantity of product stored in the inventory location.

Property.Name: isRemovalStrategy
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Removal Strategy

Property.Name: isUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: UOM of the quantity of product stored in the inventory location.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The operation at which the work was performed. If required, this field is meant to be used as an edit check to reduce the possibility that a user entered the wrong container name.

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: New Subclass of NDO used to store/allocate the material to a resource.

Property.Name: isBOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A bill of material defines the materials needed to produce a specific product.

Property.Name: isContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: isContainerChange
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: isInventoryLocation is a New Subclass of NDO used to store/allocate the material inventory to the correct location on the shoplfloor. This new object could represent a cabinet, refrigerator, desiccator, room etc.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Container or Lot selection from inventory locations

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Product used to validate the materials being added to the material queue are valid options for the Products BOM or ERPBOM

Property.Name: isERP
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Send To ERP

Property.Name: isERPBOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A bill of material (BOM) defines the materials needed to produce a specific product. An ERP BOM references steps in an ERP route instead of referencing steps in an InSite workflow.

Property.Name: isERPRoute
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ERP Routes are the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. The ERPRoute object in InSite is meant to be a mirror of the route definitions in the ERP, where the definition stored in the ERP is the "master" and the InSite ERPRoute is populated via LiveConnect. The ERPRoute is used to be able to relate InSite Moves and ComponentIssues to the ERPStep where the transaction occurred. Steps in an ERP route are usually defined at a more summarized level than is true for steps in an InSite workflow.

Property.Name: isIgnoreValidateQueue

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: isInventoryLocation is a New Subclass of NDO used to store/allocate the material inventory to the correct location on the shoplfloor. This new object could represent a cabinet, refrigerator, desiccator, room etc.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Is Kitting

Property.Name: isKitting
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: isKittingMfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: isManualConsumed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Manually Consumed

Property.Name: isMaterialListProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: isMaterialQueue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: New Subclass of NDO used to store/allocate the material to a resource.

Property.Name: isMfgOrder

Property.Name: isMfgOrderChange
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field has created like DTO objet (trensfering data to SQL) for isKittingMfgOrder field

Property.Name: isOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: isOperationChange
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: Carrier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: RecipeList
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The equivalent of TaskList for MasterRecipe.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

NavigationProperty.Name: CurrentContainerStatus
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Current status information of a Container

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: NonconformanceReport
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The NonconformanceReport (NCR) is used to track Non-conforming material. It includes attributes for analytic data (Failure, Cause, Resolution, etc) as well as attributes to identify the material that failed (Container and component information).

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: Initiator
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Close
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is used to specify whether or not a container will be closed after the execution of the transaction. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the status of the container will be set to 2 (= closed) following the move transaction. An example of when a container is closed, is when the container is shipped to the customer/distributor.

Property.Name: ContainerLevelName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Container levels are used to define a type of container, and will typically denote the position of the container within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Lot, Wafer, and Die would be defined as container levels. Attributes of the Container Level are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels.

Property.Name: ContainerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for the container

Property.Name: ContainerStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: ExistingContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: ShipmentDestination
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A ShipmentDestination is the factory or customer to which the container is shipped. ShipmentDestinaiton also contains routing information used by the RemoteProcessingInfo object when the Ship transaction is sending remote transactions to a destination site.

Property.Name: ToCustomer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Customer that the Container is being shipped to.

Property.Name: ToFactory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to identify the factory that the container is being moved to. Used by "Ship" transactions.

Property.Name: ToLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to identify the physical location that the Container is being moved to. Locations define physical areas within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute.

Property.Name: ToResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field indicates which resource the container is being moved to. A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

Property.Name: ToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object refers to the Workflow Step where the container is being moved to. If a path is provided, the path will override any information entered here. If no path or step is provided, pathselectors for the step will be evaluated to determine which path will be used. If no path selectors are valid, the container will be moved to the step referenced by the default path in the workflow.

Property.Name: ToWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: ToWorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a list of workflow steps in the workflows leading to the ToStep.

NavigationProperty.Name: Container
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) . A Container represent a grouping of other containers. The grouping allows a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. Containers are most often grouped together so a single workflow-oreiented transaction such as a move, movein, or transfer applies to the entire group of containers.

NavigationProperty.Name: CurrentStatus
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The Current Container Status contains the current location information for one or more containers. Every container associated in a multilevel container structure will have a reference to a single Current Container Status CDO.

NavigationProperty.Name: RemoteStart
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Slave service called when the container being received does not exist on the receiving site. RemoteStart is executed on a remote site. It is used to create a container or a multi-level container structure.

NavigationProperty.Name: Ship
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Slave service called when the container being received already exists

Property.Name: Capacity
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Carrier Capacity

Property.Name: CarrierContainers
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: ContainerList
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: ContainerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the Container

Property.Name: ContainerStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration to define allowed status of a container 0 - Any 1 - Good 2 - Failed

Property.Name: CreateCarrier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: InProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Is the tracking container currently in process at the current step

Property.Name: isCarrier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

Property.Name: isCarrierLoadType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration for Carrier Load Type 1 - Load 2 - Unload 3 - Setup 4 - Clear Setup

Property.Name: NextSlotPosition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Next un-filled slot on carrier

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ReuseTrackingContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Contols whether tracking container should be re-used

Property.Name: SlotPosition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Carrier Slot Position

Property.Name: SlotPositionSelection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Slot Position Selection

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: TransferContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A flag to allow container transfer. When enabled, the container will be automatically unloaded from the current carrier and loaded to the new carrier.

Property.Name: UnloadAll
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A flag to indicate that all containers will be unloaded

Property.Name: UsePosition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Use Position

Property.Name: UseQueue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Does the Operation of the Tracking Container use a queue

Property.Name: WorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.

NavigationProperty.Name: Associate
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The Associate transaction is used to create the connection between a parent container and its child container(s). This allows the user to perform subsequent Move-type transactions on the newly associated parent.

NavigationProperty.Name: CarrierChanges
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

NavigationProperty.Name: CarrierMaint
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

NavigationProperty.Name: Disassociate
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The Disassociate transaction is used to remove the connection between a parent container and its child container(s). This allows the user to either perform subsequent Move-type transactions on each child, (independently), or to associate each child with another parent container.

NavigationProperty.Name: isStart
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Start is used to create a container or a multi-level container structure.

NavigationProperty.Name: MoveIn
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The Move In service changes the container status from "In Queue" to In Process." Specifically, it sets the "InProcess" attribute of the container to "True". The Move In service is only required when the "Use Queue" option is set to "True" for the operation.

NavigationProperty.Name: MoveNonStd
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A MoveNonStd will move a container from one operation to another without regard to the current location. In other words, there does not need to be a path leading to the new location.

NavigationProperty.Name: Transfer
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Transfer is used to Transfer containers to another step and resets the CurrentThruput quantities. It does not indicate to InSite that the container has been processed at the current step, whereas MoveStd, MoveNonStd, and Rework indicate the container has been processed.

Property.Name: ActiveMfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: Availability
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Defines the current availability status for a Resource. Valid values and their meanings are:
1 = Up (Available) 2 = Down (Not available)

Property.Name: isOEELossCategory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the modeled Loss Category based on the selected Resource Status Code

Property.Name: isRecipe
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A subclass of Document describes recipe.

Property.Name: PartExpiryDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The expiry date for the part.

Property.Name: PartQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The quantity for Part resources.

Property.Name: PhysicalLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents the physical location within a factory.

Property.Name: PhysicalPosition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents the positions within a PhysicalLocation.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Product Definition describes a product to the application. This may be a Product to be manufactured, raw materials, finished, etc. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ResourceChangeCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is used to implement data concurrency.

Property.Name: ResourceGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Named Object Group that represents a group of Resources.

Property.Name: ResourceState
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource State definition: 1. NonScheduled 2. UnscheduleDown 3. ScheduleDown 4. Engineering 5. Productive 6. Standby

Property.Name: ResourceStatusCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).

Property.Name: ResourceStatusModel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This setup is used to control Resource status change as well as automated change if a pre-condition is met. It also has a list of valid Reasons the Resource can change to.

Property.Name: ResourceStatusReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Resource Status Reason Code is used to provide an added level of detail describing the reason for the current status of a Resource. For example, the current status may be REPAIR. A Status Reason Code can be used to provide additional details such as the type of repair that is being performed. This detail is included in the transaction history, which makes it available for Analysis Reporting.

Property.Name: Run
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user may specify a unique Batch ID to identify a specific production run to associate to one or more containers.

Property.Name: Setup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The configuration of a resource (hardware and other options that take significant time to change) that is now in place, at the completion of this transaction.

Property.Name: SkipStatusModelAutoSetChild
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether to skip the StatusModelDetail's automatic setting of ChildResources status.

Property.Name: SkipStatusModelAutoSetParent
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether to skip the StatusModelDetail's automatic setting of ParentResource status.

Property.Name: SkipStatusModelVerification
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag used to skip StatusModel verification.

Property.Name: Tools
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Setup the tools for the Resource. If a Tool Plan is assigned to the Resource, it will be used to verify the tools loaded.

Property.Name: ToolsInUse
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the tools the resource is currently using.

Property.Name: UpdateLastStatusChangeDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Valid values = { 1, 2, 3 }. This value determines if the value of LastStatusChangeDate gets updated or not. A value of 1 indicates to update the LastStatusChangeDate if any of the following is true: valid reason, status, run, or setup. A value of 2 indicates to update LastStatusChangeDate under all conditions. A value of 3 indicates no update to the LastStatusChangeDate.

Property.Name: UpdateParams
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether to update the Params field.

Property.Name: UpdateTools
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether to update the Tools.

NavigationProperty.Name: ResourceStatusHistory
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: System field used to generate history for the service. This field shoud not be set by the user.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used by JobProgress to trigger JobClockOff if set to true.

Property.Name: AutoClockOn
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used by JobAcknowledge to trigger JobClockOn if set to true.

Property.Name: AutoCompleteMaintenance
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether to automatically trigger the CompleteMaintenance service to complete the maintenance statuses assigned to the job.

Property.Name: CauseCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Cause Code used during a Job Progress to identify the cause identified.

Property.Name: EstimatedDuration
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The estimated duration to complete the job.

Property.Name: ExpectedStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The expected start date to work on the job.

Property.Name: Job
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the jobs that have been created from the JobOrder through JobCreate. All job transactions after JobCreate will use this object to execute.

Property.Name: JobModel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines the flow of moving the resource from one stage to another.

Property.Name: JobModelDetailDocumentSet
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the Document Set for JobModelDetail.

Property.Name: JobModelDocumentSet
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the Document Set for the Job Model.

Property.Name: JobOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Links a Job Model to one or more Equipment. Each of the Equipment can have multiple Jobs and each Job can have multiple Equipments. The Equipment cannot process a lot if there is at least one incomplete job. Also at any one time, the Equipment can be processed in one Job but all jobs must be completed and/or cancelled before the Equipment can be used for production.

Property.Name: JobStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the Job Status.

Property.Name: JobStatusExpected
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Comma delimited Job Status the transaction is allowed to transact with. A null value will not be verified.

Property.Name: JobType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the type of job (i.e. from JobModel's JobType).

Property.Name: RepairCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Repair Code used during a Job Progress to identify the repair done.

Property.Name: RequireCauseCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether Cause Code is required.

Property.Name: RequireRepairCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether Repair Code is required.

Property.Name: RequireSymptomCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether Symptom Code is required.

Property.Name: ResourceFamily
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used for selection purpose.

Property.Name: ResourceGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used for selection purpose.

Property.Name: Stage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines the various stages within a JobModel.

Property.Name: StageSequence
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the sequence of the stage within the JobModel.

Property.Name: SymptomCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Symptom Code used during a Job Progress to identify the symptom.

Property.Name: ToStage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines the various stages within a JobModel.

Property.Name: ToStageSequence
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The sequence of the next stage within the JobModel.

NavigationProperty.Name: Checklist
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Optional checklist for each detail record.

NavigationProperty.Name: ChecklistSelection
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used to return the checklist selection required for the JobProgress.

NavigationProperty.Name: MaintenanceStatuses
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the maintenance status records for the Job.

NavigationProperty.Name: MaterialList
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the material list from the Resource and MaintenanceReq BOMs.

NavigationProperty.Name: RequestOrders
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the request order used by PartTxn services.

NavigationProperty.Name: ServiceDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Service detail used for job control transactions.

NavigationProperty.Name: Technicians
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: List to assign one or more technicians to the JobOrder.

NavigationProperty.Name: TechniciansSelection
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the technicians assigned to the Job or JobOrder.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ClearLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This field is used to clear the Location field associated to the container being moved in.
Locations define physical areas within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute.
In some cases, such as when storage racks are used to hold containers before a particular operation, the Location (ie, Rack ID) needs to be cleared when the container is move into the operation (and onto processing equipment).

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource Family is used to differentiate between types of Resources such as Testers and Handlers.

Property.Name: isResourceFamilyName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Readable name for a resource family

Property.Name: isResourceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: REadable name of the resource

Property.Name: isRouteStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.

Property.Name: isRouteStepName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This field is used to identify the current physical location that the Container is being moved into.
Locations define physical areas within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object indicates which resource will be used to process the container. A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

Property.Name: ResourceLastProcessedContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The last container that was processed via the selected resource from a move or movein operation.

Property.Name: ToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: ToWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: ToWorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sub-Workflow Step is used to reference a Workflow from another Workfow. This allows, for example, the re-use of Workflows for Rework processing.

NavigationProperty.Name: CloseContainer
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Sets the container's status from active to close

NavigationProperty.Name: DisassociateChildrens
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Is used to disassociate children containers

NavigationProperty.Name: Hold
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Is a service used to put the container and its ancestors on hold. Held Containers cannot undergo normal processing (such transactions as MoveIn, Thruput, ChangeQty, Move, etc.). Transaction that can occur on held containers include to release, collect data, split, disassociate, and change attribute.

NavigationProperty.Name: isLoadUnloadCarrier
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: This transaction is used to load or unload containers into or from a carrier

Property.Name: ChildCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This indicates the number of direct child containers associated to the parent container. This field is used for qty balancing in V1.4, when compound transactions link a move with ChangeQty.

Property.Name: ClearToWorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag is used when the ToWorkflowStack list field is meant to be cleared.

Property.Name: Close
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is used to specify whether or not a container will be closed after the execution of the transaction. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the status of the container will be set to 2 (= closed) following the move transaction. An example of when a container is closed, is when the container is shipped to the customer/distributor.

Property.Name: EquipmentCycleTimeMS
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Equipment cycle time in milliseconds.

Property.Name: IPLTimeDone
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The done time value to transmit to the IPL system. Example output format is as follows: '2019-07-07T10:00:07.1035578+03:00'

Property.Name: isCarrierToLoad
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

Property.Name: isCompletedWIPSummary
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object stores the final information for all containers that have completed processing. This table is populated when a container is moved to a step where IsLastStep = true. This summary will also flag the containers that were completed on time by comparing the Containers MFGOrder planned completion date to its move date into the last step. This table can be used to calculate workflow cycle times, throughput, and yield.

Property.Name: isERPOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: isIPLSendJITMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Should CIO send a message to IPL when the container is moved?

Property.Name: isIPLSendJobChangeMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Should CIO send a message to IPL when the container is moved and the MFG order for a resource has changed?

Property.Name: isRecipe
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A subclass of Document describes recipe.

Property.Name: isRecipeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Recipe Name

Property.Name: isResourceFamily
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resources Family

Property.Name: isResourceFamilyName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Readable Name for a Resource Family

Property.Name: isResourceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Readable name for a Resource

Property.Name: isRouteStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The current RouteStep for the container. This is resolved from the containers current step.

Property.Name: isRouteStepName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: isToRouteStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The RouteStep the container is being moved to. This field is resolved from the ToSteps RouteStep reference.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to identify the current physical location that the Container is being moved from. Locations define physical areas within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute.

Property.Name: MoveAllQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to indicate whether or not entire quantity of the container will be moved to the next operation. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the entire quantity of the container will be moved. A value of "false" only makes sense in the context of a compound transaction, where the user must specify the quantity to be moved, and must account for the differences using the ChangeQty service. (Available in V1.4).

Property.Name: NavigationMode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Workflow navigation mode determines whether to use a regular Path or a ReworkPath during Move transactions. Possible navigational modes are: Standard = 1 Rework = 2

Property.Name: OverrideCurrentStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The intent of this field is to enable the client application to override the current status of the container (the step where the container is located at the beginning of the transaction). If the client application sets this field to "True" the transaction will assume the container is at the operation/step the client specifies, instead of using the operation/step of the container. This field should only be used for advanced automation systems where there is a virtual certainty that the automation system holds the correct information about the current location of the container. This allows the automation system to perform moves easily after the InSite has been taken offline and brought back up for database maintenance, etc. Note that there are no history records generated for the moves "missed".

Property.Name: Path
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Path defines an allowable (Standard) move from one Step to another within a Workflow. If a path is entered here, this path will override any information entered on the "Step" field. If no path or step is provided, pathselectors for the step will be evaluated to determine which path will be used. If no path selectors are valid, the container will be moved to the step referenced by the default path in the workflow.

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A quantity of material being tracked within a container. Each quantity has a corresponding unit of measure.

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A quantity of material being tracked within a container. Each quantity has a corresponding unit of measure. This field is only used if 2 units of measure need to be tracked at once. For instance, when specifying a container one might need to record both length and weight as quantities.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object indicates which resource was used to process the container. A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

Property.Name: ResourceLastProcessedContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The last container that was processed via the selected resource from a move or movein operation.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This spec is used by the OverrideCurrentStatus function.

Property.Name: Step
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object refers to the Workflow Step where the container is currently at and being moved from.

Property.Name: ToFactory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to identify the factory that the container is being moved to. Used by "Ship" transactions.

Property.Name: ToLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to identify the physical location that the Container is being moved to. Locations define physical areas within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute.

Property.Name: ToResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field indicates which resource the container is being moved to. A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

Property.Name: ToSpecStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.

Property.Name: ToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object refers to the Workflow Step where the container is being moved to. If a path is provided, the path will override any information entered here. If no path or step is provided, pathselectors for the step will be evaluated to determine which path will be used. If no path selectors are valid, the container will be moved to the step referenced by the default path in the workflow.

Property.Name: ToWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The workflow containing the ToStep to move to

Property.Name: ToWorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the stack of subworkflow steps that lead to the current spec step.

Property.Name: TrackStepPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Boolean flag to indicate whether to track the Step Pass for the Containers.

Property.Name: UnitCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the number of unit containers within the container structure. This field is used for qty balancing in V1.4, when compound transactions link a move with ChangeQty.

Property.Name: ValidateUDI
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Validate Unique Device Identifier. Default is false for MoveTxn and true for MoveStd transaction.

Property.Name: WorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the stack of subworkflow steps that lead to the current spec step.

NavigationProperty.Name: CloseContainer
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Sets the container's status from active to close

NavigationProperty.Name: DisassociateChildrens
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Is used to disassociate children containers

NavigationProperty.Name: Hold
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Is a service used to put the container and its ancestors on hold. Held Containers cannot undergo normal processing (such transactions as MoveIn, Thruput, ChangeQty, Move, etc.). Transaction that can occur on held containers include to release, collect data, split, disassociate, and change attribute.

NavigationProperty.Name: HVComponentIssue
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Associates a Container with an HVSetup defined on a Resource. This provides a level of traceability while minimizing history records.

NavigationProperty.Name: isLoadUnloadCarrier
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: This transaction is used to load or unload containers into or from a carrier

Property.Name: ContainerLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The level of the container currently specified for thruput .

Property.Name: isResourceFamily
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource Family is used to differentiate between types of Resources such as Testers and Handlers.

Property.Name: isResourceFamilyName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Readble name for an instance of a Resources resource family

Property.Name: isResourceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Readable name of a Resource Instance

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: QtyProcessed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the quantity of the material that has been processed at the current step.

Property.Name: QtyRemaining
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The total quantity that has yet to be processed from this container. Qty Remained For Processing = Qty - AdjustedThruputQty

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object indicates which resource was used to process the container. A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

Property.Name: SummaryThruput

Property.Name: ThruputAllQty

Property.Name: UnitCount

Property.Name: CloseWhenZero
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is used to specify whether or not a container will be closed if the container qty is zero after the execution of the transaction. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the status of the container will be set to 2 (= closed) following the change quantity transaction.

Property.Name: DisassociateWhenClosed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is used to specify whether or not a container will be disassociated when it is closed. See also "CloseWhenZero" field.

Property.Name: GenerateRollups
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines whether rollup records have to be generated. Rollups are summaries for intermediate and top-level containers concerning how much quantity was changed for all the containers underneath them with this transaction.

Property.Name: isChargeToResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Allows the system to record which Resource was used to cause the quantity to change when it is different from the Resource recorded at the current Step.

Property.Name: isChargeToResourceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Charge To Resources readbale name

Property.Name: isResourceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resources Readbale name

Property.Name: RecordAllQtySummaryOnly
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: When using the RecordAllQty function, this flag indicates whether to write history details for each of the child containers or whether a single summary record is written.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user may use this field to assign a resource at which the change quantity may be attributed to (Example: Scrap due to equipment failure). A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

Property.Name: RollupReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The reason for generating the rollup records.

Property.Name: ThruputReportingLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Container Level at which to adjust thruput, to account for quantity changes that happened before processing versus after processing. For correct functioning, must match the ThruputReportingLevel used by the Thruput transaction. Typically this field gets its value from a CVE that looks up the ThruputReportingLevel from the operation, and users are not allowed to update this field.

Property.Name: ThruputSummary
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines whether to adjust the thruput qtys of the top-level container if necessary, to account for quantity changes that happened before processing versus after processing. For correct functioning, must match the value used by the Thruput transaction. Typically users are not allowed to update this field.

NavigationProperty.Name: isStart
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Start is used to create a container or a multi-level container structure.

NavigationProperty.Name: ServiceDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The individual items a user inputs to specifically explain why the quantity is being changed.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides a way to turn on (AllowZeroQtys is False) the validations that Qty have to be greater than Zero.

Property.Name: AutoNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: AutoNumberRule
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to define auto numbering rule.

Property.Name: ChildContainers
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The list of containers to be moved to the ToContainer

Property.Name: CloseWhenEmpty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If set to True, the FromContainer will be closed when the quantity reaches zero.

Property.Name: Documents
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Document Entry is used to include a Document in a Document and provide a description for it within the Document Set. If there is more than one Document within a Document Set when a request is made to display a Document Set, the list of Document Entries is used to build a selection list. (Note that a one-to-one relationship between a Document Set and a Document is likely the common scenario).

Property.Name: ReduceQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides way to reduce qty and qty2 from the parent container. The default value for this field will be true. If this field set to false, the Qty and Qty2 for the parent container will not be reduce after split.

Property.Name: ToContainerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The name of the container to hold the split off containers/material.

NavigationProperty.Name: ToContainerDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: System field used to generate history for the service. The user should not set this field.

Property.Name: AllowZeroQtys
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides a way to turn on (AllowZeroQtys is False) the validations that Qty have to be greater than Zero.

Property.Name: ApplyStepFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: AutoLoadPhantomMaterials
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Controls whether Phantom Product BOMs will be automatically loaded for the ServiceDetails Selection Values

Property.Name: BillControl
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if this particular transaction should query for material line-item records or accept these on-the-fly

Property.Name: bpBatchContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Container representing the batch container being produced. Used to make expressions easier from modeling

Property.Name: bpFromContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used by Batch Processing to get the From Container being issued since it will always be a single container per transaction. This makes it easier for users to use in expressions for calculating required quantites.

Property.Name: bpIntermediate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Task List for task defined as a bpWeighIssue

Property.Name: bpIntermediateQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Qty the intermediate task should produce

Property.Name: IssueDifferenceReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Describes the reason for the difference between the required quantity and the actual quantity issued.

Property.Name: PhantomBillIdList
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Listof Phantom Bill Ids that have been loaded

Property.Name: PhantomQtyIssuedListTmp
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: PreventOverIssue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: When true, this value will prevent over-issuing to a material requirement if AllowOverConsumption is false on the material requirement.

Property.Name: QtyIssuedListTmp
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: ResolvedMfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: zMaterialListItemSettings
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Holds default information for the Component Issue Light transaction's Material List

NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The object is used to issue components based on the provided information.

Property.Name: ChargeToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Normally, a change in quantity is noted immediately. However, in some cases, a test performed at a step may show that an earlier step caused a change in quantity. This field allows the system to note the step that caused the quantity to change.

Property.Name: ContainerLevelInspected
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Definition of the ContainerLevel to which the ContainersInspected count field refers.

Property.Name: ContainersInspected
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Count of the number of containers inspected that resulted in the defects being recorded by this transaction.

Property.Name: isCheckDefectMapping
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Boolean to control whether any Defect Mapping should be checked

Property.Name: isDefectMapping
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defect Mapping

Property.Name: isisDefectReasons
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: List of Defect Reasons that have been used during the transaction

Property.Name: isOpenFailDefectCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Open Fail Defect Count

Property.Name: IssueActualsHistory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the list of history details for each issue to the container.

Property.Name: Qty2Inspected
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Amount of quantity inspected that resulted in the defects being recorded by this transaction, when the container is being tracked under multiple units of measure at once.

Property.Name: QtyInspected
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Amount of quantity inspected that resulted in the defects being recorded by this transaction.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This object indicates which resource will be used to process the container. A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

NavigationProperty.Name: AttachDocumentDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The details used to display the attached documents.
