Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: Sequence
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Sequence pulled from the Task.

Property.Name: Step
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Task
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The TaskListDetail from the TaskList that was processed in the service.

Property.Name: TaskComments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Comments entered by the user to describe the Task processed.

Property.Name: TaskList
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The TaskList in which the Task is defined.

Property.Name: TaskListInstruction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Instruction pulled from the Task.

Property.Name: TaskType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The TaskType pulled from the Task. 1 = Start Process Task 2 = End Process Task 3 = Regular Process Task

Property.Name: TrainingReqGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Training Requirement Grouppulled from the Task.

Property.Name: ValueAdd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates it is a value add task; used for reporting

Property.Name: VariantTaskLists
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Non-persistent field used to resolve the variant task lists

Property.Name: VariantTasks
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Proxy field to resolve tasks from the variant expressions

Property.Name: WorkCell
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The WorkCell in which the Task was processed.

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Workstation at which the Task was processed.

NavigationProperty.Name: ComponentIssue
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Component Issue is used to select and (optionally) track which raw material lots or subassemblies were used at a particular manufacturing step. The correct components to issue and the proper quantities are indicated by the Material List CDO collection of the Bill of Material. Another variation of component issue is an issue from “floor-stock”. In this case, material is decremented against a location or bin not a container. InSite should support both material issues as defined in a Bill structure ( Bill Control condition ) as well as material issues that are not specified in a predefined BOM ( Non-Bill Control condition ).

NavigationProperty.Name: DocumentEntries
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The list of Documents assigned to the Container's current Spec.

NavigationProperty.Name: IssueActualDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: This field can be used to send in a single, flat issued component to the service. Prior to any other processing for the service, the appropriate requirement will be retrieved, and an issue detail/issue actual will be built from the requirement/issued component in the normal format of the service. It is expected that this field would be useful for the case that only one issued component is passed in, or where the service is running from an interface that doesn't provide state management for the requirements.

NavigationProperty.Name: ProcessListDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Details for each ProcessItem in all ProcessLists for the Spec associated with the specified Container.

NavigationProperty.Name: ProcessSequenceValidation
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Encapsulates TaskList/Task validation logic as it relates to sequence of Tasks/TaskList completion.

Property.Name: AcceptableRejectCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Acceptable Reject Count

Property.Name: AllowedRejects
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current number of Allowed Rejects for the Sample Test for the container undergoing inspection. If the Reject count is greater than this number the SampleTest will be marked as failed.

Property.Name: AQLLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Describes the number of Rejects allowed for a specific AQL level for a given Sample Size. Each instance of this object represents an Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) value that is assigned to a Sample Plan (i.e. 0.25, 1.5, 4.0, etc.).

Property.Name: ContainerSampleData
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to record all sampling plan data for a container. The sampling plan data is stored in this objects in order to keep updates from a user to the SamplingPlan from changing once the container has started its sampling plan tested. This is also used to provide selection data for the user on the Collect Sampling transaction. The next container will pick up the new changes.

Property.Name: ContainerSampleDataItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to record all sampling plan data for a container. The sampling plan data is stored in this objects in order to keep updates from a user to the SamplingPlan from changing once the container has started its sampling plan tested. This is also used to provide selection data for the user on the Collect Sampling transaction. The next container will pick up the new changes.

Property.Name: FailedSamples
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Failed Samples

Property.Name: InspectionLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each instance of this object maintains a set of quantity ranges and their associated Lot Size Code to be assigned to a Sample Plan.

Property.Name: MoveContainerOnCompletion
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag to determine whether to move the container once sampling completed and passed

Property.Name: PassedSamples
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Passed Samples

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: Step
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: Path
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Path defines an allowable (Standard) move from one Step to another within a Workflow. If a path is entered here, this path will override any information entered on the "Step" field. If no path or step is provided, pathselectors for the step will be evaluated to determine which path will be used. If no path selectors are valid, the container will be moved to the step referenced by the default path in the workflow.

If no path selectors are valid, the container will be moved to the step referenced by the default path in the workflow.

A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. Property.Name: Close
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field specifies if the container was closed at the end of the execution of the transaction. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the status of the container was set to 2 (= closed) following the transaction. An example of when a container is closed is when the container is shipped to the customer/distributor.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: MoveAllQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to indicate whether or not the entire quantity of the container was moved to the next operation. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the entire quantity of the container was moved. A value of "false" only makes sense in the context of a compound transaction, where the user must specify the quantity to be moved, and must account for the differences using the ChangeQty service. (Available in V1.4).

Property.Name: Path
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The path actually used by the service. This path could have been input by the user, determined from path selector evaluation, or determined by the path marked as the default path for the WorkflowStep where the container was located at the beginning of the transaction.

Property.Name: Step
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the step from which the container was moved.

Property.Name: ToLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The current physical location in the factory that the Container is being moved to.

Property.Name: ToResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field indicates which resource the container was moved to. A resource is defined as a non-WIP entity which needs to be tracked/measured, such as a machine, person or storage location.

Property.Name: ToSpec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: ToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Workflow Step where the container was sent. This step could have been input by the user, or determined based on the path that was used.

Property.Name: ToStepUsage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Not currently implemented.

Property.Name: BillOfProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: Customer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Customer refers to a company that receives goods and services. A Customer definition typically refers to a company other than your own, but it can also be used for a factory or department that requires goods and services from another factory or department within the enterprise.

Property.Name: DueDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: DueDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: ExpirationDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date/time after which the Container is no longer considered first quality.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Factory often represent a physical or logical plant. A Factory can be any division, department, section, or group that is separated for accounting and reporting purposes. A Factory often represents a physical manufacturing building.

Property.Name: IssueConditionHistDetails
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: History Details for the list of Issue Conditions on Container Maintenance.

Property.Name: Level
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: Name
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: PlannedProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: PlannedQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: PlannedQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: Priority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An instance of a Priority Code is one method used to assign a processing priority to a Container. Each Priority Code includes a description and a Relative Priority value. The Relative Priority value is used to sequence Containers for dispatching (independent of the Code name or description). Priority Codes are only one of the algorithms used to determine a numeric value for Scheduling and Dispatching.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ProductionIdentifier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Production Identifier (PI) a conditional, variable portion of the UDI that identifies one or more of the following when included on the label of a device: a. Lot Number b. Serial Number of a Device c. Expiration Date d. Manufacturing Date e. D

Property.Name: RelativePriority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a numeric value that is used to sequence Containers for Dispatching ("What do I work on next?"). There are multiple algorithms that can be resolved to a single numeric value. This (use of a field) is a simple approach to dividing the algorithm from the Dispatching.

Property.Name: RemainingProcessTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Remaining Process Time value, used for RPT calculation.

Property.Name: RequestDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: RequestDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: SalesOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sales Order defines a quantity of product expected by a customer by a date. This equates to a line item on a typical (ERP) Sales Order. Containers are optionally assigned to a Sales Order (by specifying the Sales Order as an attribute). This provides the mechanism for relating WIP (Containers) to Customer Orders.

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Code. Start Codes are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).

Property.Name: isInspectUser
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: isLotNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Records the container or other manufacturing unit when the component is not tracked in InSite

Property.Name: isMfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: isOldValue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The last version of the defect before it was updated. For resolves this can be a list of defects that were resolved.

Property.Name: isOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: isProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: isRefDes
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference designator of the defect

Property.Name: isRepairDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date defect was last repaired

Property.Name: isRepairNotes
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Additional information collected from operator about repairing the defect

Property.Name: isRepairOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: isRepairResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: isRepairSpec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: isRepairUser
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: isRequireDefectReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: To identify if a Defect Reason is required

Property.Name: isResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: isSeverity
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Subclass of UserCode. Every IsDefectReason must have an associated severity.

Property.Name: isSpec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: isStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
The current status of the defect
0 = Open 1 = Repaired

Property.Name: isUpdateDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date the record was last updated, which may be different than the Create or Repair date

Property.Name: isWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: isWorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.

Property.Name: isY
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Y-axis coordinate of a board defect or short marker

Property.Name: FromBatch

Containers are most often grouped together so a single workflow-oreiented transaction such as a move, movein, or transfer applies to the entire group of containers.

Property.Name: FromLocation

Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: BillOfProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: BinSize
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of the size of the bin required to hold the material

Property.Name: ConsumingOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Consuming order

Property.Name: Customer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Customer refers to a company that receives goods and services. A Customer definition typically refers to a company other than your own, but it can also be used for a factory or department that requires goods and services from another factory or department within the enterprise.

Property.Name: DateCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date Code

Property.Name: Description
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: DeviceIdentifier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A portion of the UDI (Unique Device Identifier) that identifies the labeler and the specific version or model of a device. These unique identifiers are obtained by and FDA accredited issuing agency ( GS1, HIBCC, and ICCBBA).

Property.Name: Direction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Direction material is inserted - 0, 90, 180, 270

Property.Name: DueDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: DueDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: ExpirationDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date/time after which the Container is no longer considered first quality.

Property.Name: ExpirationDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date/time after which the Container is no longer considered first quality.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Factory often represent a physical or logical plant. A Factory can be any division, department, section, or group that is separated for accounting and reporting purposes. A Factory often represents a physical manufacturing building.

Property.Name: IssueCondition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used internally to loop through Issue Conditions

Property.Name: IssueConditions
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Issue Condition is used to control the issuance of components that are tracked as Containers using Issue Control - Issue Container (Bulk) or Issue Container (Serialized).

Property.Name: LeadFree
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Is the container product free of lead

Property.Name: Level
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: mdTeamTrackingActivityGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A User Code Object Group that represents a group of Team Tracking Activities.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: MfgPartNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Manufacturer Part Number

Property.Name: Name
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: NickName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Alternate name for container

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: PlannedProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: PlannedQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: PlannedQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: Priority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An instance of a Priority Code is one method used to assign a processing priority to a Container. Each Priority Code includes a description and a Relative Priority value. The Relative Priority value is used to sequence Containers for dispatching (independent of the Code name or description). Priority Codes are only one of the algorithms used to determine a numeric value for Scheduling and Dispatching.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ProductionIdentifier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique Device Identifier

Property.Name: RelativePriority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a numeric value that is used to sequence Containers for Dispatching ("What do I work on next?"). There are multiple algorithms that can be resolved to a single numeric value. This (use of a field) is a simple approach to dividing the algorithm from the Dispatching.

Property.Name: RemainingProcessTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Remaining Process Time value, used for RPT adjustment.

Property.Name: RequestDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: RequestDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: SalesOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sales Order defines a quantity of product expected by a customer by a date. This equates to a line item on a typical (ERP) Sales Order. Containers are optionally assigned to a Sales Order (by specifying the Sales Order as an attribute). This provides the mechanism for relating WIP (Containers) to Customer Orders.

Property.Name: SamplingLot
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to associate a group of containers for sampling. For example, an Incoming inspection lot where multiple containers are from the same lot of material, received at different times but has one AQL Sampling.

Property.Name: SamplingRequired
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if sampling is required for this container. Sampling is required when value is true

Property.Name: ShapeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the shape of the material

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Code. Start Codes are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).

Property.Name: Supplier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Supplier of container

Property.Name: SupplyFromName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Alternate name for how the material arrived in the package

Property.Name: SupplyFromType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Describes how the material arrived - reel, bulk, tube, tray, etc.

Property.Name: TxnAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used internally to map to history details.

Property.Name: UDI
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique Device Identifier

Property.Name: UOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: UOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: VendorItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Vendor Items are the products the vendor sells. This item is specified in the Product where, for purchased products, one can relate the product to a list of sources where the product can be purchased. In addition, when issuing components to a container, one can specify the VendorItem used to fulfill the component requirement.

Property.Name: isCreateDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date defect was initially created

Property.Name: isCurrentDefects
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This CDO tracks the current version of any defect associated with a container. When the isDefect service or a subclass is used to add a defect, a new version of a defect, or resolve as defect it updates the isCurrentDefect values on the container

Property.Name: isDefectLabel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defect Label

Property.Name: isDefectReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reason for the defect

Property.Name: isDefectReasonDescription
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of isDefectReason

Property.Name: isDefectType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defect Type from production client

Property.Name: isGUID
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Hexadecimal representation of GUID ( e.g. BDE4B634-153E-4A31-A453-EEA85FE80532)

Property.Name: isInitialStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
When defects are logged with this reason, this field defines the status of the defect. Value should default to OperatorChoose.
0 = Open 1 = Repaired 2 = OperatorChoose

Property.Name: isInspectNote
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Additional information about the defect

Property.Name: isInspectUser
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: isLotNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Records the container or other manufacturing unit when the component is not tracked in InSite

Property.Name: isMfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: isNewDefectReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: New defect reason used to update the defect reason for an existing defect.This value is required to perform the defect reason update.

Property.Name: isOldHistDetail
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Keep track of history details of defect details

Property.Name: isOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: isProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: isRefDes
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference designator of the defect

Property.Name: isRepairDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date defect was last repaired

Property.Name: isRepairNotes
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Additional information collected from operator about repairing the defect

Property.Name: isRepairOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: isRepairResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: isRepairSpec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: isRepairUser
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: isRequireDefectReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: To identify if a Defect Reason is required

Property.Name: isResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: isSeverity
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Subclass of UserCode. Every IsDefectReason must have an associated severity.

Property.Name: isSpec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: isStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
The current status of the defect
0 = Open 1 = Repaired

Property.Name: isUpdateDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date the record was last updated, which may be different than the Create or Repair date

Property.Name: isWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: isWorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.

Property.Name: isX
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: X-axis coordinate of a board defect or short marker

Property.Name: isY
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Y-axis coordinate of a board defect or short marker

NavigationProperty.Name: AttachDocument
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: AttachDocument is a subclass of GenericTxn that is used to attach documents to any Container, NDO, or RDO object type. There are three ways to attach a document: 1. As a reusable document that can be attached to multiple instances of an object 2. As a document that will not be reused and is only attached to a single instance of an object 3. As a reference to an existing Document

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identified whether validation of the tolerances may be overridden. If overridden the validations around the tolerances will be ignored.

Property.Name: ManualWeightEntry
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Boolean when true flags the weight will be manually entered. Used for volumetric measurements or when the scale cannot be connected to a computer.

Property.Name: ManualWeightOverrideEsignature
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ESignature requirement required for Manual Weight override entry.

Property.Name: MatchByProductName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Boolean field used to determine if the user should match by name or actual revision.

Property.Name: MaterialFromSameContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag that when checked validates that multiple issues of the same material are from the same Container or Lot

Property.Name: MaximumQuantityAllowed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expression used to calculate the maximum acceptable weight. This expression takes precedence over expression defined on the product or the material list item.

Property.Name: MinimumQuantityAllowed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expression used to calculate the minimum acceptable weight. This expression takes precedence over expression defined on the product or the material list item.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Product to weigh. This will be used to match the material list item.

Property.Name: QuantityAdditive
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Boolean when set to true updates the Batch Containers quantity with the issued products quantity.

Property.Name: RequiredQuantityExpression
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expression used to calculate the required weight. This expression takes precedence over expression defined on the product or the material list item.

Property.Name: RoundingRule
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: 1 = Round Down (Floor) 2 = Round Up (Ceiling) 3 = Round to Nearest

Property.Name: ScaleGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: List of scale groups that can be used to weigh this material. This definition takes precedence over the scale group defined on the Spec, Product or Product Family.

Property.Name: ToleranceOverrideEsignature
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Esignature requirement required when Tolerance overrides are allowed

Property.Name: ACEStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure) Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.
Value Name Meaning 1 ACESuccess after commit event completed successfully 2 ACEFSuccess an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully 3 ACEFFail an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event > 99 <custom status> User specific status codes (Designer based)

Property.Name: ChannelAdapterName

Property.Name: CIOAdapter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).

Note that the query definition is defined as instance data; the query itself can be used to retrieve information from either instance data tables or metadata tables. Field UserQueryParameters will be implemented as a persistent list so that the parameter sequence will be automatically maintained by the corresponding persistent list table.

Property.Name: ACEMessage

Property.Name: ACEStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure) Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.
Value Name Meaning 1 ACESuccess after commit event completed successfully 2 ACEFSuccess an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully 3 ACEFFail an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event > 99 <custom status> User specific status codes (Designer based)

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user performing the data entry, used primarily for security validation. If not input, security is based on the login user.

Property.Name: ChannelAdapterName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Adapter to send the outbound message. Set by CVE.

Property.Name: CIOAdapter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).

Field UserQueryParameters will be implemented as a persistent list so that the parameter sequence will be automatically maintained by the corresponding persistent list table.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String list of Condition Query Results. Populated with an OGV that executes the CIOConditionQuery so that it could used in a outbound condition expression.

Property.Name: TxnDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the service was performed. If left blank InSite uses the database system clock to determine the transaction date.

Property.Name: WhereUsed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A list of this type is returned by the Where-used functionality of a maintenance service. Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expanded property for working with Key functionality.

Property.Name: WhereUsedConfig
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Configuration object used in object upward dependency search.

Property.Name: ACEMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ACEMessage field contains the success or failure messages of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitFailure) On unhandled errors in these events, System automatically populates this field with the resolved error message.

Property.Name: ACEStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure) Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.
Value Name Meaning 1 ACESuccess after commit event completed successfully 2 ACEFSuccess an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully 3 ACEFFail an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event > 99 <custom status> User specific status codes (Designer based)

Property.Name: EffectivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This date/time is used in a comparison against EffectiveDates in modeling entities to help determine if the object should be considered for processing. This value is always specified as GMT time.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user who will get credit for the work performed. Not necessarily the user who is logging the transaction.

Property.Name: IsRemoteService
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Allows to alter standard processing of a Service in case it's executed as a Remote Service.

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: Password
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NT login password for the user performing the service, if "User" was entered. If "user" is not entered security is based on the InSite login.

Property.Name: ServerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The server name that processed the transaction.

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user performing the data entry, used primarily for security validation. If not input, security is based on the login user.

Property.Name: ChannelAdapterName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Adapter to send the outbound message. Set by CVE.

Property.Name: CIOAdapter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).

Property.Name: CIOAdapterName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: CIO Adapter Name

Property.Name: CIOConditionQuery
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Predefined query defined using the Web Modeler application or using the new Web UI infrastructure and stored as Instance Data. Note that the query definition is defined as instance data; the query itself can be used to retrieve information from either instance data tables or metadata tables. Field UserQueryParameters will be implemented as a persistent list so that the parameter sequence will be automatically maintained by the corresponding persistent list table.

Property.Name: CIOConditionResult
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String list of Condition Query Results. Populated with an OGV that executes the CIOConditionQuery so that it could used in a outbound condition expression.

Property.Name: DataVersion
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value is supposed to be saved on the client side and then resubmitted back to prevent conflicts caused by simultaneous updates of existing modeling entities. This field was introduced because the XMLAppServer supports only stateless services. This field should not be used in a stateful environment like DCOM AppServer.

Property.Name: ESigDetails-Expanded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expanded property for working with Key functionality.

Property.Name: ESigRequirement
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Contains the list of signatures that should be collected in a single transaction.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The factory where the work was performed. The container must exist in the factory specified here. Usually this field is not input by the user.

Property.Name: SyncName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The name of the object that we will try and resolve so it can be synced.

Property.Name: TxnDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the service was performed. If left blank InSite uses the database system clock to determine the transaction date.

Property.Name: WhereUsed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A list of this type is returned by the Where-used functionality of a maintenance service. An instance of this CDO will specify one of the objects using the object to change. The fields in this CDO are used to populate a tree view displayed while maintaining a modeling object.

Property.Name: WhereUsed-Expanded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expanded property for working with Key functionality.

Property.Name: WhereUsedConfig
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Configuration object used in object upward dependency search.

Property.Name: ACEMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ACEMessage field contains the success or failure messages of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitFailure) On unhandled errors in these events, System automatically populates this field with the resolved error message.

Property.Name: ACEStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure) Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.
Value Name Meaning 1 ACESuccess after commit event completed successfully 2 ACEFSuccess an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully 3 ACEFFail an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event > 99 <custom status> User specific status codes (Designer based)

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Message Contents from the CIO Message Service

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: GUID representing a CIO Message - inbound

Property.Name: Comments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Free-form text notes the user can provide when performing a service.

Property.Name: EffectivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This date/time is used in a comparison against EffectiveDates in modeling entities to help determine if the object should be considered for processing. This value is always specified as GMT time.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user who will get credit for the work performed. Not necessarily the user who is logging the transaction.

Property.Name: IsRemoteService
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Allows to alter standard processing of a Service in case it's executed as a Remote Service.

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: Password
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NT login password for the user performing the service, if "User" was entered. If "user" is not entered security is based on the InSite login.

Property.Name: ServerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The server name that processed the transaction.

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user performing the data entry, used primarily for security validation. If not input, security is based on the login user.

Property.Name: ChannelAdapterName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Adapter to send the outbound message. Set by CVE.

Property.Name: CIOAdapter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).

Property.Name: CIOAdapterName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: CIO Adapter Name

Property.Name: CIOClientGatewayURL

Property.Name: CIOConditionQuery
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Predefined query defined using the Web Modeler application or using the new Web UI infrastructure and stored as Instance Data. Note that the query definition is defined as instance data; the query itself can be used to retrieve information from either instance data tables or metadata tables. Field UserQueryParameters will be implemented as a persistent list so that the parameter sequence will be automatically maintained by the corresponding persistent list table.

Property.Name: CIOConditionResult
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String list of Condition Query Results. Populated with an OGV that executes the CIOConditionQuery so that it could used in a outbound condition expression.

The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The name of the object that we will try and resolve so it can be synced.

Property.Name: TxnDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the service was performed. If left blank InSite uses the database system clock to determine the transaction date.

Property.Name: WhereUsed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A list of this type is returned by the Where-used functionality of a maintenance service. Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expanded property for working with Key functionality.

Property.Name: WhereUsedConfig
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Configuration object used in object upward dependency search.

Property.Name: ACEMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ACEMessage field contains the success or failure messages of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitFailure) On unhandled errors in these events, System automatically populates this field with the resolved error message.

Property.Name: ACEStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure) Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.
Value Name Meaning 1 ACESuccess after commit event completed successfully 2 ACEFSuccess an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully 3 ACEFFail an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event > 99 <custom status> User specific status codes (Designer based)

Property.Name: EffectivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This date/time is used in a comparison against EffectiveDates in modeling entities to help determine if the object should be considered for processing. This value is always specified as GMT time.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user who will get credit for the work performed. Not necessarily the user who is logging the transaction.

Property.Name: IsRemoteService
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Allows to alter standard processing of a Service in case it's executed as a Remote Service.

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: Password
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NT login password for the user performing the service, if "User" was entered. If "user" is not entered security is based on the InSite login.

Property.Name: ServerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The server name that processed the transaction.

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user performing the data entry, used primarily for security validation. If not input, security is based on the login user.

Property.Name: ChannelAdapterName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Adapter to send the outbound message. Set by CVE.

Property.Name: CIOAdapter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).

Property.Name: CIOAdapterName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: CIO Adapter Name

Property.Name: CIOConditionQuery
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Predefined query defined using the Web Modeler application or using the new Web UI infrastructure and stored as Instance Data. Note that the query definition is defined as instance data; the query itself can be used to retrieve information from either instance data tables or metadata tables. Field UserQueryParameters will be implemented as a persistent list so that the parameter sequence will be automatically maintained by the corresponding persistent list table.

Property.Name: CIOConditionResult
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String list of Condition Query Results. Populated with an OGV that executes the CIOConditionQuery so that it could used in a outbound condition expression.

Property.Name: TxnDate

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A list of this type is returned by the Where-used functionality of a maintenance service.
